evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析, 午; lines 120–127
evidence.text: The database interprets the oracle graph as a wooden stick used for pounding rice and as the early graph of 杵. It describes the oracle shape and later bronze changes, reports competing whip and reins interpretations, and cites 賢簋’s 「唯九月初吉庚午」 as a bronze use of 午 for the seventh earthly branch. The page does not date this vessel or establish the implement’s ancient name or pronunciation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 漢字甲骨部件分析

gaps: No image is proposed. The four linked CUHK oracle records returned no readable text, so their pixel content and dates could not be verified. The exact Commons candidate description page and direct image were inaccessible, leaving file identity and reuse rights unverified.

CUHK supports a pestle interpretation and quotes an undated bronze branch-use example. This pass did not establish a first dated attestation or the pictured implement’s ancient name and pronunciation.

limitations.text: The CUHK paleographic account describes an oracle form interpreted as a pounding stick and later graphic changes, but its linked glyph records yielded no readable descriptions and the Commons candidate page could not be inspected. No direct image with verified identity and reuse terms is available for selection in this pass.
